This post-hoc exploratory analysis included patients from the TRUST trial with available vascular imaging data, categorized in the LVO and the non-LVO group. Each group was further divided into the UK thrombolysis group and the BMT group. Primary efficacy outcome was the proportion of patients achieving a modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score of 0-1 at 90 days. Safety outcomes included symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (sICH) within 36 h and all-cause mortality within 90 days. Of the 999 patients enrolled in the TRUST trial, 605 were included in the current study. UK thrombolysis was not associated with a 90-day excellent functional outcome in minor stroke patients, either in LVO patients (adjusted risk ratio [RR] 1.90, 95% CI 0.63-2.26) or in non-LVO patients (adjusted RR 1.02, 95% CI 0.84-1.23) compared with the BMT group (p for interaction = 0.41). In the LVO group, UK thrombolysis showed a non-significant trend toward reduced mortality (adjusted RR 0.04, 95% CI 0.01-1.65), whereas no such effect was observed in non-LVO patients (adjusted RR 0.52, 95% CI 0.11-2.52). No significant interaction was found between groups (p for interaction = 0.25). In addition, there were no patients who experienced sICH in subgroup analysis. This subgroup analysis found no improvement in 90-day functional outcomes with UK thrombolysis in minor stroke patients, irrespective of LVO presence, while maintaining a comparable safety profile with regard to mortality and sICH.
